publicPayload.contextBody: Thanks for the targeted triage-automation fix. I found a few edge cases in the deterministic checks that can still let the same regressions slip back in; the suggestions below keep the new behavior while making the tests and detection stricter.

items.title: Count action-bearing clauses instead of raw verb tokens
items.body:
### Count action-bearing clauses instead of raw verb tokens

**Severity:** `medium`

The expanded verb list currently counts every matching word, so one sentence such as "Make a key remap" contributes multiple markers (`make` and `remap`). That can classify descriptive prose as `SUFFICIENT` whenever Actual Behavior is populated. Anchoring matches to the start of a listed step or punctuation-separated clause preserves the intended natural-language support without treating repeated words in the same clause as separate reproduction steps.

```suggestion
            r"(?:^|[.!?;\n]\s*)(?:(?:\d+[.)]|[-*])\s+)?"
            r"(?:now|then|next|after(?:wards| that)?|try(?:ing)?(?: to| and)?)?\s*"
            r"(?:(?:open|launch|click|press|select|enable|disable|connect|disconnect|type|drag|run|choose|restart|create|make|configure|remap|hold|use)|(?:i|we|you|users?|the user)\s+(?:can\s+|will\s+|try\s+to\s+)?(?:open|launch|click|press|select|enable|disable|connect|disconnect|type|drag|run|choose|restart|create|make|configure|remap|hold|use))\b",
```

items.title: Cover generic prose and concise action-clause variants
items.body:
### Cover generic prose and concise action-clause variants

**Severity:** `medium`

The new heuristic needs both positive and negative coverage: generic prose with repeated action words should not satisfy the reproduction gate, while concise first-person or semicolon-separated action sequences should. These cases pin the intended clause-level behavior and protect the added `make`/`use` support from regressing.

```suggestion
    def test_natural_language_shortcut_reproduction_is_sufficient(self):
        body = BUG_BODY.replace(
            "1. Open Keyboard Manager.\n"
            "2. Select Remap a shortcut.\n"
            "3. Press a key and observe that the editor closes.",
            "Make a key remap, (alt (left) + tab), then try and use it. "
            "It's disabled!\n\n"
            "Now hold alt + tab, then press w, or any other key. It activates it.",
        ).replace(
            "The editor exits.",
            "Alt+Tab still functions when using other keys alongside it.",
        )
        self.assertEqual(CONTEXT.reproduction_quality(body), "SUFFICIENT")

    def test_generic_prose_with_repeated_action_words_is_insufficient(self):
        body = BUG_BODY.replace(
            "1. Open Keyboard Manager.\n"
            "2. Select Remap a shortcut.\n"
            "3. Press a key and observe that the editor closes.",
            "I use Keyboard Manager every day and make shortcuts often. "
            "It is useful when I use my keyboard.",
        ).replace(
            "The editor exits.",
            "The shortcut does not work as expected.",
        )
        self.assertEqual(CONTEXT.reproduction_quality(body), "INSUFFICIENT")

    def test_first_person_reproduction_steps_are_sufficient(self):
        body = BUG_BODY.replace(
            "1. Open Keyboard Manager.\n"
            "2. Select Remap a shortcut.\n"
            "3. Press a key and observe that the editor closes.",
            "I open PowerToys Settings. Then I select Keyboard Manager.",
        ).replace(
            "The editor exits.",
            "The Keyboard Manager page does not load.",
        )
        self.assertEqual(CONTEXT.reproduction_quality(body), "SUFFICIENT")

    def test_semicolon_separated_reproduction_steps_are_sufficient(self):
        body = BUG_BODY.replace(
            "1. Open Keyboard Manager.\n"
            "2. Select Remap a shortcut.\n"
            "3. Press a key and observe that the editor closes.",
            "Open Settings; then click Keyboard Manager.",
        ).replace(
            "The editor exits.",
            "The Keyboard Manager page does not load.",
        )
        self.assertEqual(CONTEXT.reproduction_quality(body), "SUFFICIENT")

    def test_first_person_make_and_use_sequence_is_sufficient(self):
        body = BUG_BODY.replace(
            "1. Open Keyboard Manager.\n"
            "2. Select Remap a shortcut.\n"
            "3. Press a key and observe that the editor closes.",
            "I make a key remap. Then I use it.",
        ).replace(
            "The editor exits.",
            "The remapped shortcut does not activate.",
        )
        self.assertEqual(CONTEXT.reproduction_quality(body), "SUFFICIENT")
```

items.title: Constrain the actual label mutation call inventory
items.body:
### Constrain the actual label mutation call inventory

**Severity:** `medium`

The current contract only blocks the removed variable names, so the workflow could reintroduce version-label mutations under renamed variables and still pass. Checking the actual `addLabels` and `removeLabel` call arguments enforces the stated contract directly for both the source workflow and generated lockfile.

```suggestion
    def test_workflow_never_manages_version_labels(self):
        import re

        def label_call_arguments(workflow, method, argument):
            calls = re.findall(
                rf"github\.rest\.issues\.{method}\(\{{(.*?)\}}\);",
                workflow,
                re.DOTALL,
            )
            return [
                match.strip().removeprefix("[").removesuffix("]").strip()
                for call in calls
                for match in re.findall(rf"{argument}:\s*([^,\r\n}}]+)", call)
            ]

        source = WORKFLOW_SOURCE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        generated = WORKFLOW_LOCK.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        for workflow in (source, generated):
            self.assertNotIn("versionLabels", workflow)
            self.assertNotIn("desiredVersionLabel", workflow)
            self.assertEqual(
                sorted(label_call_arguments(workflow, "addLabels", "labels")),
                sorted(["'Needs-Author-Feedback'", "desiredProductLabel"]),
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                label_call_arguments(workflow, "removeLabel", "name"),
                ["'Needs-Author-Feedback'"],
            )
        self.assertRegex(source, r"never adds or removes\s+version labels")
```
